title: Supreme Court: An Arbitration Clause Cannot Divert a Consumer Complaint Already Admitted by a Forum
case_name: T.K.A. Padmanabhan v. Abhiyan Cooperative Group Housing Society Ltd., through its Secretary
citation: Civil Appeal No. 10724 of 2016, judgment dated 4 June 2026
card_summary: A Delhi housing society member's consumer complaint over delayed possession was admitted by the District Forum; the society then invoked the agreement's arbitration clause to push it out. The Supreme Court held an admitted consumer complaint cannot be diverted to arbitration merely because the agreement has an arbitration clause, and restored the complaint for decision on merits within a year.
card_tip: An already-admitted consumer complaint cannot be pushed into arbitration just by pointing to a clause in the agreement; that clause does not defeat the forum's jurisdiction on its own.
verification_notes: Selected for Consumer Protection because the interplay between arbitration clauses and consumer forum jurisdiction is a recurring, high-search question for homebuyers across Delhi NCR, and the dispute itself originated in a Delhi housing society matter (District Consumer Forum, New Delhi), giving it a direct Delhi angle. Case name, Civil Appeal No. 10724 of 2016, the 4 June 2026 date, and the core holding (arbitration clause cannot oust an already-admitted consumer complaint, following the Fair Air Engineers v. N.K. Modi line of authority) are confirmed across three independent reports (LiveLaw, SCC Online, Verdictum). The precise original forum's name varies between sources (District Consumer Forum-VII, New Delhi, versus District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Dwarka) and is therefore not stated specifically. Not previously covered on the site, which has general RERA-versus-arbitration guides but not this specific Supreme Court ruling on admitted consumer complaints.
